item.text: `tsx` is using an IPC server internally, which is what the sandbox is blocking. I’m doing one last pass on the new files and a more precise untracked listing for the source directory so the final report is explicit about what was verified and what the environment prevented.
I found one avoidable cast in the test file. I’m removing it so the implementation is the only place using the single narrow `fields.value` cast that matches the current `index.ts` behavior.

The code is settled. I’m rerunning the typecheck after that cleanup and using a direct `node --import tsx` fallback to validate the test file logic, since the `npx tsx` wrapper itself is what the sandbox blocks.

Added [`evaluate-runtime.ts`](/home/thduy-h/mnt/d/THANHDUY/SheCanCode/packages/lesson-engine/src/evaluate-runtime.ts) and [`evaluate-runtime.test.ts`](/home/thduy-h/mnt/d/THANHDUY/SheCanCode/packages/lesson-engine/src/evaluate-runtime.test.ts). The new evaluator is pure, uses the shared types, mirrors the runtime semantics from `index.ts`, and throws for the four block-structure variants instead of handling them.

Verification:
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/lesson-engine` exited `0`.
- `node --import tsx src/evaluate-runtime.test.ts` in `packages/lesson-engine` exited `0` and printed `evaluate-runtime tests passed`.
- `npx tsx src/evaluate-runtime.test.ts` could not be verified in this sandbox because `tsx` tried to open an IPC pipe and failed with `EPERM`.
- `git status --short --untracked-files=all -- packages/lesson-engine/src/evaluate-runtime.ts packages/lesson-engine/src/evaluate-runtime.test.ts` shows exactly those two new files. Repo-wide `git status --short` does not show only two files because the repository is currently broadly untracked.

Explicit confirmations:
- The `"5"` vs `5` normalization is preserved via `comparableValue`, which trims strings, converts finite numeric strings to numbers, and otherwise normalizes text.
- The `if_print` hybrid is preserved: it requires both matching output and a matching `print` child under the found `if` block.
- These four variants throw with message prefix `evaluateRuntimeLogic does not handle block-structure variant:`:
  `required_block_types`, `ordered_block_types`, `max_top_level_blocks`, `variable_name`.
